scenes.heading: The Cartesian plane
scenes.sub: Two numbers that pin down any spot
scenes.say: How can two numbers tell you exactly where something is? Maps, games and graphs all use the same idea: a grid called the Cartesian plane.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Cinema ticket: walk along to seat 7, then up to row D
scenes.science: Point (x, y): go across x, then up or down y
scenes.breaks: Cinema seats start at 1, but the plane also goes left of zero and below zero with negative numbers.
scenes.say: Think of a cinema ticket. The seat number tells you how far along to walk, and the row tells you how far up to climb. Two numbers, in a set order, find exactly one seat. Coordinates work the same way: across first, then up or down.

scenes.heading: The grid
points: y-axis: up and down. Up +, down −
Point (x, y): x first, then y
scenes.say: The x-axis goes across: right is positive, left is negative. The y-axis goes up and down: up is positive, down is negative. They cross at the origin, zero zero. A point is written x first, then y.

scenes.heading: The four quadrants
scenes.say: The axes split the grid into four quadrants, numbered anticlockwise from the top right. The first has both coordinates positive. The second, top left, has negative x. The third has both negative. The fourth, bottom right, has negative y.

scenes.heading: Moving a point
scenes.question: Start at (−3, 2). Move 5 right and 6 down. Where are you?
scenes.say: Start at negative three, two. Move five right and six down. Right changes x: negative three plus five is two. Down changes y: two minus six is negative four. You end at two, negative four.
scenes.caption: Start at (−3, 2). Move 5 right and 6 down. Right changes x: −3 + 5 = 2. Down changes y: 2 − 6 = −4. You end at (2, −4).

scenes.heading: Area of a rectangle
scenes.question: Find the area of the rectangle with corners (−3, 2), (4, 2), (4, −1), (−3, −1).
scenes.say: Find the area of this rectangle. Across, from negative three to four, you cross zero, so add: seven units. Up, from negative one to two: three units. Seven times three is twenty-one square units.
scenes.caption: Find the area of this rectangle. Across, from −3 to 4, you cross zero, so add: 7 units. Up, from −1 to 2: 3 units. 7 × 3 = 21 square units.

scenes.heading: Reflecting a point
scenes.say: Reflecting in the x-axis flips a point up and down, so the y-coordinate changes sign. Reflecting in the y-axis flips it left and right, so the x-coordinate changes sign.

points: Along the corridor, then up the stairs
Negative x is left, negative y is down
Quadrants go anticlockwise from top right
Crossing zero? Add the two parts
scenes.say: Quick recap. Along the corridor, then up the stairs. Negative x is left, negative y is down. Quadrants go anticlockwise from the top right. And when a distance crosses zero, add the parts. Now try the practice questions!
